item.title: Electric Propulsion Database Development and Integrated Modelling Analysis
item.description: arXiv:2611.13121v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Electric propulsion (EP) systems require significant subsystem integration and data driven mod- elling for accurate sizing. This paper is an overview of a high-fidelity database development and analysis aiming to fill the gap in electric propulsion sizing. This is a preliminary study to develop a tool that considers all thruster technologies that exist within Electric Propulsion. Since thrust is set by the product of efficiency and available electrical power, this paper showcases that thruster selection directly constrains the spacecraft power bus. We showcase and hypothesize within the database analysis and in the future work that the correct way to choose electric propulsion systems is through budgeting the EP system through Mission constraints. Comparing technologies for propulsion parameters is important for spacecraft optimisation and no such dataset exists. The literature offers either deep surveys of one thruster type, which cannot be compared across technologies, or broad catalogues that quote manufacturer figures at a single operating condition without checking whether those figures agree with one another. This paper reports the development, performance levels and preliminary analysis of a unified Electric Propulsion technology database. Every device is reduced to a common set of parameters including power, thrust, specific impulse, exhaust velocity and total efficiency linked by governing analytical equations and state space models. The database holds 390 distinct models from 22 countries across twelve thruster types, from 0.4 W to 1 MW, with first flights from 1964 to 2025.
item.dc:creator: Talha Baig, Dr Kate Smith, Dr Nicholas Crisp

item.title: Constraining electron heat flux from reduced measurements
item.description: arXiv:2611.14340v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Coronal heating estimates depend partly on electron heat transport. Different electron velocity distributions can match the same observations yet carry different heat fluxes. We ask which measurements are enough to determine heat flux without finding how electrons are distributed across all speeds and directions. The solar wind carries electrons outward from the corona and allows their velocities to be measured directly. Using one Wind measurement, we keep density, mean flow, temperature and angular summaries for each energy channel. In the fixed-bin model, electron distributions that match these quantities have heat fluxes from 3.58 to 19.85 $\mu$W m$^{-2}$. Keeping the correlation between electron motion along and across the magnetic field fixes the heat flux at 11.73 $\mu$W m$^{-2}$, matching the original bin calculation. This recovers heat flux without reconstructing the full shape of the electron velocity distribution. When the measured counts vary, retaining the required correlations leaves the same heat-flux range as direct calculation from those counts. We propose testing coronal observations in the same way to find which features of electron motion they constrain well enough to determine heat transport. Those constraints could help establish the heating requirements used to assess coronal heating mechanisms.
item.dc:creator: Victor Edmonds

item.title: Nucleation of water ice under weak ionization via clustering on negative ions
item.description: arXiv:2611.14441v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Water-ice grains are shown to form spontaneously in a cold, weakly-ionized laboratory plasma with trace water admixture when neutrals and ions are cooled below $\sim$200 K. These conditions serve as an analog of ice nucleation in cold astrophysical and atmospheric environments. The ice grains form without the presence of particulate impurities, and do not form in the absence of ionization, indicating that nucleation is induced by ions. Time-resolved ion mass spectrometry provides separate detection of clusters of water molecules on both positive and negative ions. Hydrated negative ions, mainly $\mathrm{OH^-(H_2O)_n}$, grow to $\sim$200 amu, while hydrated positive ions, mainly $\mathrm{H^+(H_2O)_n}$, remain small and short-lived. As the temperature is reduced from room temperature toward 200 K, negative ion clusters grow in size and then drop sharply in abundance, consistent with the onset of rapid growth into macroscopic ice grains below a critical temperature. This indicates that hydrated negative ions are key precursors to ice nucleation in cold, weakly ionized environments, such as the Earth's mesosphere and protoplanetary disks, providing a concrete pathway for ice formation in environments where the nucleation mechanism has remained unresolved. This negative ion pathway is estimated to dominate over ice deposition on pre-existing dust grains in protoplanetary disk locations where there is sufficient UV to partially dissociate water molecules, and in addition, where negative ions such as OH- can form readily through electron attachment at low temperature.
item.dc:creator: Andr\'e Nicolov, Efstratios M. Kritikos, William A. Goddard III., Paul M. Bellan

item.title: Gravitational radiation from a particle in circular orbit around a wormhole: the nonrotating case
item.description: arXiv:2611.14455v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we have generalized Poisson's(1993) calculation for the case of gravitational radiation from a particle in a circular orbit around a black hole to the case of the wormhole. Considering the motion of a test particle around a Schwarzschild like wormhole and using Teukolsky formalism, we have obtained an analytical result of flux at infinity under the assumption of small velocities. Focusing on the 22-mode, we have found a novel 0.5PN order term beyond the quadrupole order, which vanishes in the black hole limit. On the other hand, all higher order terms are getting modified in such a way that they give correct correspondence in the black hole limit. We have further corroborated our results with the numerical investigations, which show that the two waveforms match well when the particle lies far from ISCO. Thus, our work provides one of the first attempts toward the study of the post-Newtonian waveforms involving wormholes (ECOs).
